verdict.summary:
Solid feature, but two things block merge.

1. **Guaranteed crash on capture.** `charge.ts:42` calls a Stripe method that does not exist, so every capture throws.
2. **Undisclosed auth change.** The session TTL jumps from 1h to 30d with no mention in the PR body.

The Payments area also needs boundary tests before this ships.

groups.name: Payments
groups.reason: Mutates billing state and calls the Stripe API.

scorecard.note: No unchecked casts; new types in `types.ts` match the SDK shapes.
Violates the repo's error-handling rule — empty catch swallows declines.
`charge.ts` mixes validation, API calls, and mapping in one 210-line function.
Backend logic is covered on the happy path only (see Test gaps).

findings.title: Calls undefined Stripe.captureIntent()
findings.evidence:
The Stripe Node SDK groups calls by resource: payment intents live under `stripe.paymentIntents.*`, and the method that finalizes an already-authorized charge is `capturePaymentIntent()`. There is no `captureIntent()` — so this call can never succeed. ## What the code does `src/pay/charge.ts:42` calls a method that doesn't exist: ```ts const res = await stripe.captureIntent(intentId); // not a function ``` Every capture request funnels through that one line, so the failure is total: ## Why it always breaks JavaScript only notices a missing method *when the line runs* — there's no compile-time check catching it here — so it sailed through review and then throws the instant a capture happens: | Call | In the SDK? | Result | | --- | --- | --- | | `stripe.captureIntent(id)` | no | `TypeError` at runtime | | `stripe.capturePaymentIntent(id)` | yes | captures the charge | A grep of the installed types confirms it: ```text $ grep -rc captureIntent node_modules/stripe/types 0 ```
Impact
Because every capture path runs this one line, the feature fails 100% of the time — this is a guaranteed crash, not an edge case.

findings.title: Stripe error swallowed by empty catch
findings.suggestion: Re-throw or return a typed failure so callers can react to declines instead of always seeing `ok: true`.

findings.title: Session TTL raised from 1h to 30d, not mentioned in PR
findings.evidence:
The PR body describes **only** the Stripe capture flow. But `src/auth/session.ts:15` also raises the session lifetime by ~720×:

```diff
-const SESSION_TTL = 3600;      // 1 hour
+const SESSION_TTL = 2592000;   // 30 days
```

Why this matters: the session TTL is how long a stolen cookie stays usable. Going from 1 hour to 30 days widens that window enormously — a real security trade-off that reviewers approving "a Stripe change" would never notice.
findings.suggestion: Confirm this is intentional. Either document it in the PR description or split it into a separate, reviewable change.

findings.title: Amount not validated before hitting Stripe
findings.evidence: `charge(amount)` forwards `amount` straight to Stripe without checking it is a positive integer within the allowed ceiling. A negative or absurdly large value reaches the payment API unchecked.
findings.suggestion: Validate `1 <= amount <= 999999` before the API call.

findings.title: left-pad@1.3.0
findings.evidence: Used **once** in `src/util/fmt.ts:12` to pad a 3-char code. Last published 2018.

findings.title: stripe@14.2.0
findings.evidence: Actively maintained, widely used, no known advisories at this version.

findings.title: No test at the 999999-cent ceiling
findings.evidence: charge() should reject amounts over 999999 but no test exercises the boundary.

findings.title: Declined-card path untested
findings.evidence: A test covers a successful capture but none asserts behavior when Stripe returns `card_declined`.
findings.suggestion: Add a test that stubs a declined charge and asserts the caller sees a failure.

findings.title: No test for zero-amount charge
findings.evidence: Behavior for `charge(0)` is unspecified and untested.
findings.suggestion: Decide and assert whether `charge(0)` is rejected.

findings.title: Set STRIPE_SECRET_KEY in production
findings.evidence: stripe.ts:4 reads process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY; the app will fail to boot without it.
findings.suggestion: Add `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` to the production secret store before deploy.

findings.title: Watch session store size after TTL increase
findings.evidence: Raising session TTL to 30d will grow the session store; monitor memory/row count post-deploy.
findings.suggestion: Add a dashboard alert on session store growth.

findings.title: Empty catch violates the error-handling convention
findings.rule: docs/conventions/error-handling.md: no empty catch — re-throw or return a typed failure

findings.title: charge() mixes validation, I/O, and mapping in one 210-line function
findings.evidence:
`charge()` handles input validation, the Stripe call, and response mapping in a single ~210-line function.

## The rule

`docs/conventions/readability.md` targets functions under ~60 lines and suggests separating I/O from pure transformation. This is a **SHOULD**, so it's a nudge, not a blocker.

```text
$ awk '/function charge/,/^}/' src/pay/charge.ts | wc -l
210
```
findings.suggestion:
Pull `validateAmount()` and `mapChargeResult()` out as small pure helpers, leaving `charge()` to orchestrate. Smaller units are easier to unit-test (see the Payments test gaps).

Takeaway: separating pure logic from I/O is what lets you test the tricky branches without stubbing the network.
findings.rule: docs/conventions/readability.md: functions under ~60 lines; separate I/O from transformation

findings.title: Optional `metadata` dereferenced without a null check (pattern, 4 sites)
findings.evidence:
`ChargeInput.metadata` is optional (`src/pay/types.ts:8`), but four call sites dereference it unguarded — any charge created without metadata throws `TypeError`.

```ts
const tag = input.metadata.orderTag; // metadata may be undefined
```

All four sites repeat the same shape; this is one systemic gap, not four separate bugs.
findings.suggestion:
Guard the access (`input.metadata?.orderTag`) or make `metadata` required at the validation boundary.

Takeaway: an optional field makes every unguarded dereference a claim that someone upstream checked — grep the call sites before trusting it.

locations.note: make `metadata` required here, or document why it is optional
pass an empty object default instead of dereferencing

findings.regradeNote: Grouped by the arbiter: 4 findings of the same missing-null-check class collapsed into one; severity set once for the class.

findings.title: `fmtAmt` abbreviation diverges from the spelled-out naming convention
findings.evidence: `docs/conventions/naming.md` prefers spelled-out names (`formatAmount`) over abbreviations; `src/util/fmt.ts:9` adds `fmtAmt`.
findings.rule: docs/conventions/naming.md: prefer spelled-out names over abbreviations

findings.title: Capture retry can double-charge when the first attempt actually succeeded
findings.evidence:
The retry loop re-calls capture on timeout — but a timeout does not mean the first capture failed; Stripe may have processed it. No idempotency key is passed, so a retried capture can charge twice.

No single lens owns this: it spans error handling, external calls, and operational behavior, which is why only the full-context pass surfaced it.
findings.suggestion: Pass an idempotency key on capture and treat a timeout as unknown-outcome rather than failure.
